Correction: the four provinces the page names. Shah Mahmud took Shiraz in 1364 and Shah Shoja retook it in 1366 (civil war inside the same state). The page says the kingdom at its zenith 'comprised Iranian Azerbaijan, central Persia, and Persian Iraq' without a year; the only dated Azerbaijan episodes are the brief occupations of 1359 and 1374.

Page: 'a slaughter of the populace, in the Sacking of Isfahan (1387)'.

ledger.note: 1314: Mubariz al-Din Muhammad succeeds his father Sharaf al-Din Muzaffar, governor of Maibud, and founds the Muzaffarid dynasty. Infobox 'Established: 1314'; the text names Mubariz al-Din as founder and does not connect 1314 to an event. The disambiguation page gives 1335.
About 1319: Mubariz al-Din overthrows the atabeg of Yazd and is recognised as governor of the city by the Il-Khan government ('In around 1319 he overthrew the atabeg of Yazd').

Late 1340: Mubariz al-Din takes Kerman from the Mongol governor Qutb al-Din b. Nasir ('In 1339 or 1340 he invaded the province of Kirman'; Qutb al-Din briefly retook it with Kartid help; 'Mubariz al-Din permanently gained control of Kirman in late 1340').

1352: Mubariz al-Din invades Fars after the Injuids are defeated in battle ('invaded Fars in 1352 ... laid siege to Shiraz in 1353'). The Muzaffarid page: Abu Ishaq 'defeated on the field in 1353' and fled to Isfahan.
1357: Isfahan falls and Abu Ishaq is executed at Shiraz; the Injuid war ends.
1357: 'Fars was absorbed by 1357 into the expanding Muzaffarid state'; 'The Injuid lands now fell into the hands of the Muzaffarids'.

1357: Mubariz al-Din 'laid siege to that city also, and captured it in 1357'; Abu Ishaq was executed. The Muzaffarid page leaves the year of Isfahan's fall open ('Fars and western Iran were now under his control').
After 1357 the capital is Shiraz (infobox 'Kerman, Shiraz (after 1357)').

1359: Shah Shoja 'managed to occupy Azerbaijan and Arran for four months, briefly capturing Tabriz'. The Muzaffarid page has Mubariz al-Din occupying Tabriz and retreating before Jalayirid troops after Jani Beg's conquest of 1357, undated.
1359: the four-month occupation ends; Uways returns to Tabriz (the page gives the length, four months, not the month).

1364: Shah Mahmud 'invaded Fars and captured Shiraz'; Shaykh Uways of the Jalayirids 'occupied Shiraz, capital of the Muzaffarid Shah Shoja, in support of his rival brother Shah Mahmud' (Jalayirid page).
1366: 'Shah Shoja would not be able to reconquer his capital until 1366'.

1374: when Shaikh Hussain Jalayir began his reign 'Tabriz was raided by the Muzaffarids'; the Muzaffarid page: after Uvais died in 1374 Shah Mahmud claimed Tabriz and 'occupied it briefly', dying the next year.
1374: the occupation of Tabriz is brief (the page: 'briefly'); Shah Mahmud dies 'the next year'.

1387: Timur sacks Isfahan ('a slaughter of the populace, in the Sacking of Isfahan (1387)'); Shiraz 'soon fell to Timur' and was given to Shah Yahya, and the princes rule separately until 1391. The page does not name Isfahan's holder in 1387; Shah Shoja had occupied it after 1375.

ledger.note: 1393: Shah Mansur loses the Battle of Shiraz to Timur and is beheaded; the remaining Muzaffarid princes swear allegiance, are received honourably and are executed ('on 22 May in Qumisha'). The land named is Shiraz; the provinces are my reading of the realm.

region.text: Kerman, Yazd, Fars and Isfahan, the provinces the page names as held

ledger.note: 1393: the Muzaffarid dynasty ends with the Battle of Shiraz (1393) and the execution of its princes; infobox 'Disestablished: 1393', successor Timurid Empire. Zain al-Abidin and Sultan Shibli were sent to Samarkand.

wars.name: Muzaffarid conquest of Kerman
wars.outcome: Mubariz al-Din invades Kirman in 1339 or 1340 and holds it permanently from late 1340 after Qutb al-Din briefly retakes it with Kartid aid.
wars.note: Bam was conquered 'a few years after this', undated.

wars.name: Muzaffarid-Injuid war
wars.outcome: Abu Ishaq seeks Kirman (1347), besieges Yazd (1350-51), is defeated (1353) and executed after Isfahan falls in 1357; Fars and Isfahan pass to the Muzaffarids.
wars.note: The Injuids page dates the invasion of Fars 1352, the siege of Shiraz 1353 and Isfahan 1357.

wars.name: Muzaffarid-Jalayirid wars over Azerbaijan and Shiraz
wars.outcome: Shah Shoja occupies Azerbaijan and Tabriz for four months in 1359; Uways occupies Shiraz for Shah Mahmud in 1364; Muzaffarids raid Tabriz in 1374. No border changed.

wars.name: Muzaffarid civil war of Shah Shoja and Shah Mahmud
wars.outcome: Shah Mahmud, backed by the Jalayirids, holds Shiraz from 1364; Shah Shoja reconquers it in 1366.
wars.note: Shah Mahmud ruled at Isfahan 1364-1366 on the page's ruler list.

wars.name: Sarbadar-backed revolt in Kirman
wars.outcome: 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad backs a revolt in Kirman against Shah Shuja, which fails in December 1374; Shah Mansur later sides with Amir Vali against 'Ali (1381).

wars.name: Timur's conquest of the Muzaffarids

zones.text: Kerman, Yazd, Fars and Isfahan, the provinces the page names as held

wars.outcome: Timur sacks Isfahan (1387), decides on a campaign against Shah Mansur in 1392, reaches Shushtar and Dizful by March 1393 and wins at Shiraz in 1393; the princes are executed or sent to Samarkand.

certainty.note: A regional dynasty of cities and provinces; no treaty frontier appears on any page. The Isfahan and Fars frontier with the Injuids (1357) and the Kerman frontier are approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria's Wikipedia title 'Muzaffarids' is a disambiguation page (three dynasties, the Iranian one 'from 1335 to 1393'); the Muzaffarid dynasty of Iran is the article 'Muzaffarids (Iran)', which the dossier uses as its page. 'Muzaffarid dynasty' is also a disambiguation page. Five pages cited (two of them disambiguation pages, one state article, Injuids, Jalayirid Sultanate, Sarbadars).
Cliopatria problems: (1) the state starts in 1344 but the page has it from 1314 (infobox; the disambiguation page says 1335; the text gives only 'around 1319' for Yazd and late 1340 for Kerman); new keyframes 1314-1343. (2) The 1344 and 1363-1394 shapes lack Kerman (3% and 0%), the seat after 1340, and most of Fars (0%, 23%, 22%), whose Shiraz was the capital from 1357; they carry South Khorasan, Semnan and Chahar Mahall land that no page ties to the Muzaffarids. The 1344 shape also has Isfahan 13 years before its 1357 capture. (3) The row runs to 1394, the page says 1393. (4) After 1387 the realm splits among three princes until 1391 (Shah Yahya at Shiraz, Sultan Ahmad at Kerman, Sultan Abu Ishaq at Sirajan); drawn as one state.
Not settled: whether the Muzaffarids ruled Persian Iraq and Azerbaijan for more than months (the page says so at the zenith without a year); Hormuz and Lar relations (not on the page); the date of Bam's conquest ('a few years after' 1340); Khuzestan (Timur reached Shushtar and Dizful by March 1393 and set up a Sarbadar governor, but the page does not call them Muzaffarid); the Kartid role in Kerman 1340 (undated). The Injuid page and the Muzaffarid page disagree on Isfahan: the Muzaffarid page has Abu Ishaq flee to Isfahan after 1353 where Mubariz al-Din 'took the city and executed him'; the Injuid page has the capture in 1357.
Counterparts needing dossiers: Atabegs of Yazd (overthrown c. 1319, no Cliopatria row, group me-09-x or ia-02). The Ilkhanate belongs to ia-02. The Timurid dossier (ia-02) has gain muzaffarids 1387 and 1393, consistent with the loss events here.
Gazetteer: every name resolves; 'Maibud (Meybod)' is not in places.jsonl and is stood for by a 70 km radius round Yazd (gazetteer name needed: Meybod, place, Yazd province).
